articles.title: Morocco’s ruling allies turn on each other before election campaign begins
articles.summary: Political tensions rise as Moroccans prepare for the polls, with the official campaign start still days away.
articles.body:
Morocco’s governing allies are trading accusations, politicians are switching camps and a leaked recording has exposed tensions at the top of the ruling coalition – all before the official campaign begins on September 10.

Moroccans are due to vote for a new parliament on September 23, with candidate nominations opening on August 31. By the afternoon of the first day, 702 candidate lists from 27 political parties had been submitted, according to the Interior Ministry.

About 15.8 million voters are registered for the election, according to the Interior Ministry, in a country of 36.8 million people, according to the 2024 census. The voting-age population is estimated at roughly 25 million, according to the High Commission for Planning (HCP).

The political contest is already under way, as parties finalise candidates, sharpen their messages and position themselves for a battle that will determine who has the strongest hand in forming the next government.

Moroccans will elect members of the House of Representatives, the lower house of parliament.

The party that comes first will have the strongest claim to lead the process of forming the next government. Under Morocco’s Constitution, the king appoints the head of government from the party that comes first in elections to the House of Representatives.

But coming first does not mean governing alone.

Morocco’s multi-party system means the winning party needs to negotiate with other parties and build a coalition capable of securing parliamentary support.

That makes the size of each party’s parliamentary group important, including the parties that are already governing together.

The National Rally of Independents (RNI), the Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM) and the Istiqlal Party currently form the governing coalition.

They are partners in government, but they are also rivals competing for votes, candidates and influence.

Why are governing allies already fighting?

The latest dispute has brought those tensions into the open.

A leaked audio recording attributed to House of Representatives Speaker Rachid Talbi Alami, a senior RNI figure, has exposed tensions between the RNI and PAM over budget minister and senior government figure, Fouzi Lekjaa. The recording circulated after the RNI accused PAM of attracting its elected officials and candidates.

Lekjaa is a high-profile politician in Morocco. He has headed the Royal Moroccan Football Federation since 2014 and is widely known for his role in Moroccan football, including the national team’s historic run to the 2022 World Cup semifinals and its quarterfinal appearance this year. He is also the minister delegate in charge of the budget.

In the recording, the voice attributed to Talbi Alami appears to criticise Lekjaa without naming him directly and warns against allowing him to obtain the economy and finance portfolio in a future government.

The recording has since prompted public responses from RNI President Mohamed Chouki and Head of Government, Aziz Akhannouch. He defended internal party discussions as part of political debate and said the focus should be on winning the election rather than distributing government posts in advance.

Lekjaa also responded, rejecting the idea of dividing government posts before the election, saying that “dividing up the spoils without having hunted them” was not his concern.

The issue is bigger than a dispute between two politicians.

If senior figures in governing parties are already discussing who should hold key government positions after the election, it raises a question for voters: how much of the next government is being negotiated before they have even cast their ballots?

That does not mean the election outcome is predetermined. But it shows how parties are already positioning themselves for the government that will follow the vote.

The controversy also illustrates the tension at the heart of the governing coalition. RNI, PAM and Istiqlal are partners in government today, but they are competing against one another for candidates, seats and influence.

Who are the main parties and what do they want?

The RNI, which emerged as the largest party in the 2021 parliamentary election with 102 seats, is seeking to defend its position.

PAM won 87 seats and Istiqlal 81. The three parties formed the governing coalition after that election.

The governing parties can point to economic reforms, investment and the expansion of social protection as evidence of progress. Their opponents will argue that those measures have not done enough to ease pressure on households.

Opposition parties will seek to turn dissatisfaction with the government’s record into votes, while smaller parties will compete for seats that could give them leverage in forming the next coalition.

That makes the election a contest, not only over which party comes first, but over which parties emerge with enough weight to shape the government that follows.

Can the Justice and Development Party make a comeback?

The Justice and Development Party (PJD) is one of the opposition parties to watch.

The PJD governed Morocco for two consecutive terms from 2011 to 2021, but suffered a dramatic defeat in the 2021 election, falling from 125 seats to just 13.

Despite its small parliamentary group, the party has remained a vocal critic of the government.

Its politicians have challenged it over issues such as alleged conflicts of interest, prices, employment and public services.

Under Secretary-General Abdelilah Benkirane, the PJD is seeking to rebuild its support and regain political influence.

The question is whether its visibility as a small but vocal opposition group can translate into votes.

After its collapse in 2021, the PJD faces the difficult task of convincing voters that it deserves another chance to govern.

The cost of living, employment, healthcare and education have long been among voters’ top concerns and remain so ahead of the election.

Inflation has slowed from the sharp increases seen in previous years, but the cost of everyday goods remains higher than before prices began rising rapidly.

In simple terms, prices may be increasing more slowly, but they have not gone back down. For many households, food, transport and other basic expenses, therefore, remain more expensive than they were a few years ago.

The government can point to economic growth, investment and the expansion of social protection as evidence of progress. Its opponents are likely to argue that those gains have not translated into enough relief for ordinary families.

Employment will be another major concern, particularly for young people.

Healthcare and education are also likely to feature prominently as voters assess whether government reforms have improved the public services they rely on.

For voters, the question may be less about whether economic indicators are improving than whether they can actually feel that improvement in their daily lives.

Has the government delivered on its promise to create jobs?

Employment is likely to be one of the biggest tests of the government’s record.

The government’s 2021-2026 programme pledged to create at least one million net jobs over five years. By the end of 2025, net job creation stood at about 95,000, according to an analysis by Medias24, although the government uses a different measure, saying 850,000 non-agricultural jobs were created between 2021 and 2025.

The issue gives opposition parties a powerful campaign line: whether voters should judge the government by its promises or by the employment situation they see around them.

It also raises a wider question: how much trust should voters place in promises made by politicians?

Healthcare and education are likely to be another major test of the government’s record.

The government has undertaken reforms aimed at expanding social protection and improving public services.

But its opponents continue to highlight problems in health, education and access to public services.

For voters, the issue is likely to be whether reforms have improved the services they encounter every day — from schools and hospitals to access to doctors and teachers.

Could Eid al-Adha and meat prices become an election issue?

The cost of celebrating Eid al-Adha could also become part of the political debate.

Last year, Moroccans were urged to refrain from their traditional sacrifice of sheep after drought and a sharp decline in livestock numbers pushed up prices and put the ritual beyond the reach of many families.

The issue returned this year, when sheep were again available for the holiday but prices had rocketed, making the traditional sacrifice unaffordable for many. Recent reports described widespread frustration over sheep prices, with some families saying they could not afford to buy.

For many households, the issue goes beyond a religious holiday. Rising meat prices have become part of wider concerns about the cost of living and whether families can still afford foods once within reach.

For opposition parties, Eid al-Adha and meat prices provide another opportunity to question the government’s handling of livestock supplies, food prices and household finances.

For many voters, however, the issue is simpler: whether they can afford to put meat on the table and maintain an important family tradition.

Why is the Ceuta tragedy a sensitive election issue?

The mass crossing into the Spanish-administered enclave of Ceuta on July 30 has added a sensitive issue to Morocco’s political landscape.

At least 72,000 crossed from Morocco, according to Reuters. The episode resulted in 82 deaths on the Spanish side and 14 confirmed deaths on the Moroccan. Spanish authorities said between 5,000 and 8,000 people remained in Ceuta as of August 28.

The human cost remains a major part of the story. By August 21, authorities had identified only six of those who died, according to data provided by Ceuta’s court.

The mass movement was fuelled in part by misleading information circulating on social media. Migrants told reporters they had seen posts and videos suggesting that Spain had opened its border, helping attract thousands of people towards Ceuta.

The episode has also become a diplomatic issue, with Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez saying on August 31 that there was no evidence Morocco had been involved in organising the mass crossing, while attributing the influx to criminal networks and disinformation.

The episode has therefore become more than a border and migration story. It has raised questions about the risks faced by Moroccans seeking to reach Europe and the circumstances that drove so many to attempt the crossing.

The Justice and Development Party (PJD), now in opposition, has called for a royal commission of inquiry into the mass migration attempt, bringing the episode into the political debate.

Ceuta and Melilla are Spanish-administered cities on the North African coast. Morocco considers both occupied cities and claims sovereignty over them, while Spain considers them part of its territory.

The tragedy therefore brings several issues into the election debate: youth opportunities, employment, migration, social media and Morocco’s relations with Spain.

The question is whether parties will use the incident to debate the conditions and opportunities that shape migration decisions, or whether it will remain primarily a security and diplomatic issue.

Are conflicts of interest damaging political trust?

Questions about conflicts of interest are another potential campaign issue.

The PJD has repeatedly used allegations involving links between political office and private business interests to attack the government.

For opposition parties, the issue is about transparency and accountability.

For the government, the challenge is to convince voters that public decisions are being made in the public interest.

It feeds into a wider problem: trust in politicians.

For some voters, campaign promises have not translated into meaningful improvements. Others may see politicians moving between parties or governing allies fighting over candidates and positions as evidence that political calculations come first.

Morocco’s Interior Ministry opened registration to the electoral lists during two separate periods ahead of the September 23 election.

The first was part of the annual revision of the electoral lists.

The ministry then opened an exceptional period beginning on May 15, with the final revised electoral lists established on July 10.

The ministry then opened a second, exceptional 30-day period from May 15 to June 13, allowing eligible citizens who were not registered to apply ahead of the election.

The ministry has not published a national total for new registrations made during that second period.

Interior Ministry figures reported before the election showed that citizens aged 18 to 24 accounted for about three percent of registered voters. That figure refers to registered voters, not to all Moroccans in that age group.

Registration, however, is not the same as voting.

Turnout in the 2021 parliamentary election was about 50 percent of registered voters.

The challenge for political parties is therefore not only winning votes from people who are politically active, but also persuading those who have become disengaged to participate.

How is social media shaping the campaign?

Social media is already playing a role in the political debate ahead of voting.

Political parties and candidates can reach voters directly through platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube, alongside traditional rallies, television appearances and party structures.

The platforms also allow accusations, leaked recordings and political controversies to spread quickly.

The Talbi Alami recording is one example. The audio circulated online before becoming a wider political controversy and prompting responses from figures in the RNI, PAM and the government.

Social media also played a significant role in the mobilisation around the Ceuta crossings. Al Jazeera reported that accounts on social media called on thousands of people to travel to Ceuta, while migrants told reporters they had seen videos and messages suggesting that the border had been opened.

For Morocco’s election, social media is therefore already an important arena for political messaging, controversy and the spread of information and misinformation.

The September 23 election will determine the composition of Morocco’s next parliament and set the balance of power from which the next government will be formed.

The governing parties will ask voters to judge their record. Opposition parties will argue that the government has fallen short of its promises.

But beneath the competition over seats lies a broader question: can Morocco’s political parties persuade a sceptical electorate that another election will produce meaningful change?

The governing coalition’s internal disputes may dominate headlines in the weeks ahead.

But the more consequential contest will be over jobs, prices, public services, trust, youth frustration and turnout.

The official campaign has not started, but the political contest is already under way.

articles.title: Dabo Swinney Responds to Report Lane Kiffin Leaked Ole Miss Tampering Info to Clemson HC
articles.summary: With Clemson and LSU set to face each other in Saturday's highly anticipated showdown, Dabo Swinney and Lane Kiffin will once again be under the spotlight.
articles.body:
With Clemson and LSU set to face each other in Saturday's highly anticipated showdown, Dabo Swinney and Lane Kiffin will once again be under the spotlight.

And the Clemson coach pushed back at the notion his counterpart previously gave him intel to assist in the Tigers' turning in Ole Miss for tampering when it came to linebacker Luke Ferrelli.

Swinney told reporters Wednesday any suggestion Kiffin "egged him on" and provided such intel was false. "Lane Kiffin had nothing to do with that," he added. "Zero. … People can make up whatever stories they want."

USC HC Claps Back at Attendance Criticism

In May, ESPN's David Hale and Mark Schlabach reported the NCAA opened an investigation into Ole Miss on the same day Swinney publicly accused Rebels head coach Pete Golding of tampering with Ferrelli.

"This is a whole other level of tampering," Swinney said on Jan. 23. "It's total hypocrisy. ... This is a really sad state of affairs. We have a broken system, and if there are no consequences for tampering, then we have no rules and we have no governance."

Golding replaced Kiffin as the Ole Miss head coach when the latter left for LSU before the Rebels' participated in last season's College Football Playoff.

With that as the backdrop, John Talty of CBS Sports shared an excerpt from his upcoming book Lane Being Lane: The Story of Lane Kiffin, College Football's Agent of Chaos that said Kiffin "passed along information … to help Swinney in his crusade against Golding and Ole Miss."

After Ole Miss linebacker T.J. Dottery transferred to LSU, the Rebels turned their attention to Ferrelli despite his decision to join Clemson. According to Talty, Ole Miss "offered him a significant raise over what he was expected to make at Clemson."

When Ferrelli decided to join the Rebels, Swinney went public with his tampering allegations.

Talty wrote that "Clemson offensive line coach Matt Luke, the former Ole Miss head coach, called his alma mater to give it a heads-up on what Kiffin had helped convince Swinney to do."

However, Swinney was adamant Kiffin had nothing to do with the situation during his recent press conference.

He was also asked about the NCAA's investigation into Ole Miss and said, "No, I haven't heard anything. It was true, he was in school for a week, it did happen. Then he magically ended up at another place. It really doesn't frustrate me. I am just trying to win a game this weekend. That's it. Let everybody else worry about all that stuff."

Swinney and Clemson will face Kiffin and LSU on Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET.

articles.body:
The Division I-FBS college football season started last Saturday, when Bill Belichick's UNC squad defeated TCU 15-10 in Dublin, Ireland.

Week 0 had some interesting moments, like Virginia (and new quarterback Beau Pribula) rolling over NC State 34-8 and USC quarterback Jayden Maiava authoring a great game (25-of-29, 286 yards, two scores) to lead the No. 14 Trojans to a 42-26 home win over San Jose State.

USC was the only ranked team to take the field, but college football really gets going in earnest this week, though, as the rest of the Top 25 squads (and the remaining CFB teams that didn't start yet) get going.

Here's a look at this week's schedule, odds and some picks for this week.

All odds are via FanDuel Sportsbook , and all rankings are via the Associated Press' preseason poll .

Arkansas Pine Bluff at No. 25 Missouri (-54.5), 8 p.m., SEC Network

Idaho at No. 21 Utah (-34.5), 9 p.m., ESPNU

UTEP at No. 10 Oklahoma (-41.5), SEC Network

North Texas at No. 6 Indiana (-40.5), 12 p.m., FOX

Ball State at No. 1 Ohio State (-50.5), 12:30 p.m., Big Ten Network

Tennessee State at No. 3 Georgia (-47.5), 2 p.m., SEC Network

Furman at No. 20 Tennessee (-48.5), 3:30 p.m., SEC Network

Marshall at No. 18 Penn State (-24.5), 3:30 p.m., FS1

Texas State at No. 5 Texas (-29.5), 3:30 p.m., ESPN

Boise State at No. 2 Oregon (-24.5), 3:30 p.m., CBS

Northern Illinois at No. 22 Iowa (-31.5), 4:15 p.m., Big Ten Network

Missouri State at No. 8 Texas A&M (-40.5), 7 p.m., ESPN

Abilene Christian at No. 12 Texas Tech (-42.5), 7 p.m., FS1

Western Michigan at No. 16 Michigan (-27.5), 7:30 p.m., NBC

Clemson at No. 11 LSU (-10.5), 7:30 p.m., ABC

Utah Tech at No. 14 BYU (-51.5), 8 p.m., ESPN+

Washington State at No. 17 Washington (-23.5), 4 p.m., NBC

Wisconsin at No. 4 Notre Dame (-20.5) in Green Bay, 7:30 p.m., NBC

No. 24 Louisville vs. No. 9 Ole Miss (-6.5) in Nashville, 7:30 p.m., ABC

No. 19 SMU (-3.5) at Florida State, 7:30 p.m., ESPN

SMU returns quarterback Kevin Jennings, who is entering his third season as the Mustangs' starter. During his time in Dallas, Jennings has completed 65.0 percent of his passes for 7,709 yards (8.0 yards per attempt), 55 touchdowns and 26 interceptions. He's also rushed for 559 yards and 10 scores.

SMU has gone 20-7 under Jennings' watch, and he has the benefit of playing behind a veteran-laden offensive line. Three starters are returning in center Joshua Bates, tackle P.J. Williams and guard Addison Nichols.

Although SMU has to replace a lot of rushing and receiving production, an experienced quarterback and offensive line should go a long way toward another good season for the Mustangs.

Florida State already started its season last week, defeating New Mexico State 34-17. This wasn't the easiest game for the Seminoles, which entered the contest as a 31.5-point favorite against an Aggies team that is listed at 133rd overall on the latest Sagarin Ratings .

NMSU found success through the air (272 passing yards and two touchdowns from quarterback Trey Hedden), and FSU was only up 10 (27-17) midway through the fourth quarter.

FSU bore down, scored late and got the 17-point win, but SMU presents a far greater challenge. The guess here is Jennings leads the Mustangs to a road win by at least one touchdown.

Notre Dame returns 14 starters , including Heisman Trophy candidate and quarterback CJ Carr, four offensive linemen and wide receiver Jordan Faison, who led the team with 49 receptions and 640 yards.

They also bring back eight defensive starters, including cornerback Leonard Moore, who could be one of the 2027 NFL draft's top picks.

This team looks like a national championship contender on paper, and it goes up against a Wisconsin team that is headed in the wrong direction.

The 2025 Badgers went 4-8, the team's worst record since 1990. Wisconsin isn't predicted to make a leap this year and sits 12th in the Big Ten's preseason media poll .

Wisconsin just finished second-to-last in all of Division I FBS with 12.8 points per game. Although ODU transfer and dual-threat Colton Joseph brings excitement at the quarterback position, it's asking a lot of a new-look offense to excel right away against a tough Notre Dame D.

No. 9 Ole Miss (-6.5) over No. 24 Louisville

Ole Miss is entering its first full season in the post-Lane Kiffin era under head coach Pete Golding, the former defensive coordinator who took over for the now-LSU head coach last November after he left for the Tigers.

Golding's Rebels showed great resolve and spirit despite the tremendous turmoil, defeating Tulane 41-10 and Georgia 39-34 in the College Football Playoff before falling just short to Miami, 31-27.

Now the Rebels enter the college football season with high expectations at No. 9 in the early polls. That makes sense considering the talent Ole Miss brings back, including quarterback Trinidad Chambliss and running back Kewan Lacy, who arguably make up the best offensive backfield in the country. Three offensive linemen are back as well.

Ole Miss' best player might be defensive tackle Will Echoles, who could very well be a top-10 pick in the upcoming NFL draft. He anchors a promising Rebels defense.

Echoles and the Rebels' greatest task might be stopping a potentially explosive Louisville rushing attack featuring Isaac Brown, who ran for 8.8 (yes, 8.8) yards per carry last year (884 yards, seven touchdowns on 101 carries). The Cardinals also welcome quarterback and Ohio State transfer Lincoln Kienholz, who will bring his dual-threat abilities into the mix.

The issue is deciphering how the Cardinals will slow down the Ole Miss attack. That's less a commentary on Louisville, which could absolutely be competing for a CFP spot in the ACC title game this year, and more praise for Ole Miss, which could have one of the best offenses in college football this year.

articles.title: NCAA Clears University of Cincinnati of Wrongdoing in Brendan Sorsby Gambling Investigation
articles.summary: CINCINNATI (AP) — The NCAA has cleared the University of Cincinnati of any wrongdoing in its investigation of former quarterback Brendan Sorsby.
articles.body:
CINCINNATI (AP) — The NCAA has cleared the University of Cincinnati of any wrongdoing in its investigation of former quarterback Brendan Sorsby.

Sorsby played the 2024 and '25 seasons for the Bearcats before transferring to Texas Tech. He was ruled permanently ineligible by the NCAA in April after he placed thousands of impermissible sports bets over the past four years at Indiana and Cincinnati.

"Earlier this summer, NCAA enforcement staff completed an inquiry into a former Cincinnati student-athlete's prohibited betting activity during his time at the university. The inquiry is now closed and the student-athlete was found to have committed a Level III violation," Cincinnati senior associate athletic director for communications Zach Stipe said in a statement. "Cincinnati worked closely with the NCAA throughout the process, which began when the initial reports of impermissible sports wagering began."

The Cincinnati Enquirer was the first to report on the university being cleared.

The NCAA sent an official letter of inquiry to the school regarding Sorsby in early July. That came after Sorsby's agent, Ron Slavin, said during a radio interview in Dallas that Cincinnati was aware of Sorsby's gambling.

NCAA Level III violations are attributed to Sorsby and not Cincinnati or its coaching staff. The violation was when the ProhiBet app on Sorsby's phone flagged him trying to make a bet, but he was denied access to the betting site.

UC's compliance department told Sorsby of gambling restrictions by student-athletes.

The NCAA declared Sorsby ineligible for making bets worth at least $90,000 during his college career.

Sorsby made at least 40 bets on Indiana while he was a freshman there in 2022, but none of those bets came on games in which he played. He acknowledged placing at least 165 impermissible bets on college and professional sports totaling at least $38,000 in 2024, including three wagers on Cincinnati men's basketball made on a FanDuel account he shared with a friend. He provided more than $60,000 to the friend to deposit in the shared account between December 2023 and June 2025.

Sorsby passed for 2,800 yards with 27 touchdowns and five interceptions last season. He also ran for 580 yards and nine TDs. The Bearcats started 7-1 before losing their final five games.

Cincinnati still has a pending federal lawsuit against Sorsby, accusing him of breaching his name, image and likeness contract following his transfer to Texas Tech.

articles.title: 360-degree sustainability! How Super League Kerala is trying to build Indian football from the ground up
articles.summary: Football News: NEW DELHI: For decades, Kerala has been the heartbeat of Indian football. Floodlit local tournaments draw packed crowds, school grounds produce gifted.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: For decades, Kerala has been the heartbeat of Indian football. Floodlit local tournaments draw packed crowds, school grounds produce gifted footballers, and the sport is woven into the state's cultural identity. Yet translating that passion into a sustainable professional football ecosystem has remained elusive.As the third season of the Super League Kerala (SLK) prepares to kick off on September 25, the league believes it has found a different path. Rather than chasing the glamour of bigger leagues or relying on broadcast windfalls, SLK is attempting to build what its CEO and Director, Mathew Joseph, calls a "360-degree sustainability" model, one where clubs, vendors, grassroots academies and fans all become stakeholders in the game's future.Joseph is candid that Indian football's biggest challenge isn't attracting investors, but ensuring they stay."Our focus from the beginning has been sustainability. It has just not been a sustainability for the league, but a 360-degree sustainability for every stakeholder," he tells TimesofIndia.com in a virtual conversation.The "360-degree sustainability" philosophy influences almost every decision the league makes. SLK has introduced a strict salary cap, fixed player and technical staff budgets, centralised vendors to reduce operational costs, and revenue-sharing mechanisms designed to prevent financial disparity between clubs.The entire model has been worked out in such a way that the teams, apart from the league, the next biggest stakeholder is the teams. In fact, all put together, the teams are more important than us.Last season, the combined expenditure of the league and its teams approached Rs 90 crore, with the league itself investing around Rs 30 crore while individual clubs spent between Rs eight-10 crore. The player purse has been capped at Rs 1.75 crore (±10%), while technical staff budgets are limited to Rs 25 lakh (±10%). Teams are penalised for both overspending and underspending to maintain competitive balance."The entire model has been worked out in such a way that the teams, apart from the league, the next biggest stakeholder is the teams. In fact, all put together, the teams are more important than us. Because if anyone drops out or if the profitability or the sustainability is affected, they will not stay back. There is a limit to which anyone can bring in money," explained Joseph.The economic model allows the clubs to retain 100% of their own ticketing, sponsorship, merchandise and academy revenues. Only centrally generated league income is pooled, with 40% currently distributed to clubs, while future broadcast rights would see 60% flow directly to teams.Chasing global audienceDespite its name, Joseph insists Super League Kerala has never positioned itself as a regional league."From day one, I was very clear that we are not just a regional league. I could have gone to a regional channel here and said that we are a regional league, can you broadcast us? We were with Star Sports, HotStar, Sony, Doordarshan, Sports.com, Etisalat in UAE and now we are with Zee5 (Unite8 Sports). This is for the nation. We are building up football in India," said Joseph.This year our focus has been on digital first. With Zee5 being our OTT partner, they are ready to take it across the world because most of the Indians who have smart TVs have access to Zee5. So most of the Indians and Keralaites will have access to the league.Given Kerala's large population that has settled across the world, the league looks to target an audience far beyond its borders.With large Malayali communities spread across the Middle East, Europe and North America, SLK views the diaspora as an important audience. But Joseph believes quality football can also attract supporters from neighbouring southern states.His bigger bet, however, is digital consumption."This year our focus has been on digital first. With Zee5 being our OTT partner, they are ready to take it across the world because most of the Indians who have smart TVs have access to Zee5. So most of the Indians and Keralaites will have access to the league. It should actually help us stream it better," said Joseph.Additionally, the league is looking at exploring vertical mobile broadcasts, multiple camera angles for viewers, and interactive viewing experiences tailored for smartphones, an acknowledgement that many Indian households have a single television but multiple mobile screens.Football with a guaranteed winnerPerhaps the most visible innovation this SLK season will come on the pitch.For the first time in Indian football, every group-stage match will produce a winner. If teams finish level after 90 minutes, the match goes directly to a penalty shootout. A regulation victory earns three points, a shootout win two, a shootout loss one, and a regulation defeat none.Joseph believes eliminating draws will fundamentally change the spectator experience.FIFA has given permissions to such things in Japan, China and a few other countries. So, we are introducing that and this is going to make it more interesting for any spectator or a person who is watching it on television."We will have, definitely, a decision at the end of the match. FIFA has given permissions to such things in Japan, China and a few other countries. So, we are introducing that and this is going to make it more interesting for any spectator or a person who is watching it on television," said Joseph.SLK has also expanded its knockout stage to include home-and-away semi-finals, increasing the season from 33 to 35 matches.Grassroots before glamourLong before launching the league, SLK had already invested in youth football. According to Joseph, the organisation has operated 52 academies, trained over 17,000 children, and built its own talent identification programme (Project Game Changer) in collaboration with the Andrés Iniesta Academy.Our focus for the last six years since 2020 has been to develop a grassroots (system). We had scouts present year-round at university matches, inter-school, inter-college matches.This year's scouting programme attracted around 3,500 players across six locations in Kerala, with club scouts evaluating prospects for every franchise."Our focus for the last six years since 2020 has been to develop a grassroots (system). We had scouts present year-round at university matches, inter-school, inter-college matches. Last year, out of about 2000-odd children who came, we shortlisted close to about 15, took them into camps, and finally about five of them got selected into various Super League Kerala teams," Joseph said.The league's ambition isn't merely to produce players for the top-tier Kerala Blasters."We are not a feeder system to (Kerala) Blasters. We are a feeder system, or we would love to be a feeder system, for the entire ecosystem of football across the country. It can be another regional league, it can be a national league, it can be an I-League (now IFL) or it can be ISL, anything. As long as people play and get an opportunity elsewhere, we are more than happy," Joseph said, presenting his vision.One success story is Muhammed Sinan, who emerged through Project Game Changer before becoming one of Kannur Warriors' standout performers and earning national recognition. He returns for season three alongside experienced Indian players such as Prasanth K, Abdul Hakku Nediyodath and Pragyan Sundar Gogoi, while overseas recruits include Varo Álvarez, Asier Gomez, Ernesten Lavsamba and Grace Adieu Youmou.Why foreign players matterSLK continues to mandate experienced overseas footballers and Pro Licence coaches, not simply to improve match quality but to accelerate player development."We try to bring in players who are experienced, who have better footballing knowledge, who have played with many other leagues," said Joseph.Joseph argues that young Indian footballers develop faster when surrounded by professionals who have competed across different football cultures.Season three also features accomplished coaches including Karim Bencherifa (Malappuram FC), Vital Borkelmans (Forca Kochi), Andrey Chernyshov (Kannur Warriors) and Ever Adriano Demaldé (Calicut FC), giving local players access to diverse tactical philosophies.The long gameIf Indian football is waiting for broadcasters to rescue its finances, Joseph believes it's waiting for the wrong solution. "I don't think linear television is going to pay anymore," he says plainly.Instead, SLK is exploring subscription models, season passes, pay-per-view products and nearly 20 separate revenue streams currently being structured alongside management and accounting firm KPMG. The objective is to create measurable fan commitment rather than speculative club valuations.We thought we could [expand league from six to eight teams], but we realized that in the five months' time, we will not be able to do justice to that place.He also sees infrastructure as the next frontier. The league deliberately postponed expansion from six to eight teams this year because stadiums in prospective cities weren't ready."We thought we could, but we realized that in the five months' time, we will not be able to do justice to that place," he reasoned.Ultimately, Joseph believes clubs must own or control their stadiums if they are to become genuinely valuable sporting institutions.For now, though, season three represents another important step rather than the finished product. Bigger audiences, fuller stadiums, improved technology and stronger grassroots pathways are the immediate targets.As Kerala prepares for another footballing autumn, the league's ambition extends well beyond crowning another champion. It wants to prove that Indian football's next sustainable success story can begin not in the country's biggest cities, but in the state that has loved the game the longest.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cesc Fàbregas y Nico Paz son nombrados 'Mejor Entrenador' y 'Mejor Joven' de la Serie A
articles.standfirst: 'Gran Galà del Calcio' de la Asociación Italiana de Futbolistas (AIC)
articles.summary: 'Gran Galà del Calcio' de la Asociación Italiana de Futbolistas (AIC)
articles.body: Cesc Fàbregas fue elegido mejor entrenador de la Serie A 2025-2026, mientras que el argentino Nico Paz recibió el premio al mejor jugador joven, durante la 'Gran Galà del Calcio' de la Asociación Italiana de Futbolistas (AIC). Fàbregas, técnico del Como, equipo que este año disputa Liga de Campeones por primera vez en su historia, fue reconocido como el mejor entrenador de la temporada en unos premios decididos por votación de los futbolistas, y entregados durante la noche de este miércoles en el emblemático Teatro alla Scala de Milán. Nico Paz, formado en la cantera del Real Madrid y jugador del conjunto lombardo por lo menos un temporada más, recibió el galardón al mejor futbolista joven de la Serie A. El centrocampista argentino, además, fue incluido en el once ideal de la temporada, en el que comparte ataque con el delantero del Inter Milan Lautaro Martínez y el neerlandés Donyell Malen, referencia ofensiva del Roma. El premio al mejor jugador de la Serie A fue para el defensa del Inter Federico Dimarco, y el conjunto interista, ganador del 'Scudetto' la pasada campaña, fue elegido mejor club de la temporada. El guardameta Mile Svilar, los defensas Marco Palestra, Alessandro Bastoni y Manuel Akanji, y los centrocampistas Hakan Çalhanoğlu, Scott McTominay y Luka Modric completaron el once ideal junto a Nico Paz. El 'Gran Galà del Calcio' también reconoció a Maurizio Mariani como mejor árbitro y a Mattia Liberali como mejor joven de la Serie B. El premio al mejor gol fue para el portugués del Juventus Francisco Conceiçao, un tanto de volea desde la frontal del área que se coló por la escuadra de la portería del Roma. La gala, que alcanzó su decimoquinta edición, sirvió además para homenajear a Franco Baresi, fallecido el pasado 31 de julio a los 66 años, y recordar a la selección italiana campeona del mundo en 2006, cuando se cumplen veinte años del título conquistado en Alemania.

articles.title: Aubameyang finiquita su pesadilla internacional: "Me humillaron y mancharon mi imagen"
articles.standfirst: El máximo goleador de la historia de las Panteras se retira de la selección de Gabón tras su desencuentro con el Gobierno
articles.summary: El máximo goleador de la historia de las Panteras se retira de la selección de Gabón tras su desencuentro con el Gobierno
articles.body: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, el delantero de moda en LaLiga tras su espectacular arranque de temporada en el Deportivo, ha anunciado con 37 años su retirada de la selección de Gabón. "Me humillaron y mancharon mi imagen cuando jugué la Copa Africana de Naciones lesionado. Fue la gota que colmó el vaso, y prefiero dejarlo así", explicó Aubameyang en una entrevista al programa 'Talent d’Afrique' de Canal+, apuntando a las críticas que recibió por parte de funcionarios del Gobierno tras el mal papel de Gabón en la Copa Africana de Naciones de 2025. Gabón perdió los tres partidos en la Copa África y no sumó ningún punto. Tras estos resultados el Gobierno de Gabón despidió al cuerpo técnico (Sébastien Migné es el nuevo seleccionador), suspendió a la selección nacional hasta nueva orden y culpabilizó a Aubameyang, máximo goleador histórico de 'Las Panteras' con 40 goles en 83 partidos, y Bruno Ecuele Manga del fracaso. "Es una parte de la identidad nacional la que queda debilitada", comentó Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema, el entonces presidente de Gabón. Sobre estas suspensiones Aubameyang apuntó que "creo que los problemas de la selección van mucho más allá del papel insignificante que desempeño". Tras quedar fuera del Mundial de 2026, Gabón tendrá como objetivo clasificarse para la próxima edición de la CAN, prevista en Kenia, Tanzania y Uganda del 19 de junio al 17 de julio de 2027.

articles.title: Pablo Barrios, otro salto... a la capitanía
articles.standfirst: La salida de Giménez hará que el canterano sea el cuarto en el escalafón tras Koke, Oblak y Llorente
articles.summary: La salida de Giménez hará que el canterano sea el cuarto en el escalafón tras Koke, Oblak y Llorente
articles.body: Pablo Barrios sigue dando saltos en su meteórica carrera hacia el estrellato. Capitán general de la medular rojiblanca desde hace ya varias temporadas, el canterano avanza a pasos agigantados a marcar una época como rojiblanco. Sobre su rol en el verde está todo más que contado. Es pieza angular para Simeone y sus lesiones en la segunda parte de la temporada pasada fueron determinantes para que el Atlético no terminara tocando metal. Pese a que el argentino intentó protegerle, la carga de partidos superando los 60 encuentros entre todas las competiciones acabaron en infinitas visitas a la enfermería. Tras un verano de trabajo específico, con una nueva dieta y con hábitos que ayuden a prevenir las lesiones musculares que tanto han cortado su carrera (habría ido al Mundial de no ser por ellas), el jugador da un nuevo salto en su trayectoria. Y en este caso en su peso en un vestuario en el que ya ejerce de voz autorizada. Así, si la salida de Griezmann coloca a Marcos Llorente como tercer capitán, la de Giménez (que se ha marchado cedido al Deportivo) convierte al 8 en el cuarto destinatario del brazalete tras el citado 14 y los dos grandes pesados del vestuario: Koke y Oblak. Todo ello, tras un arranque espectacular en el que ha sido uno de los más destacados de los rojiblancos. Asistió ante el Sevilla y no duda en echarse el equipo a la espalda en los momentos más duros. A los 23 años ya es un referente que, además, formará en el cuarteto de capitanes del club de su vida. Otro salto más.

articles.body: Es un partido para alejar los fantasmas del pasado y, sobre todo, para recuperar la tranquilidad. La Real Sociedad y el Celta iniciaron mal la pasada Liga y no quieren recordar en la presente esos malos tiempos y lo mucho que cuesta corregir después un comienzo complicado de campeonato. Por eso, los donostiarras reciben esta noche a los gallegos en el estadio de Anoeta con el deseo de lograr su segunda victoria consecutiva ante su afición e ir hacia arriba en la clasificación, alejándose de una parte baja de la que el conjunto vigués, al que aún se le resiste el triunfo, quiere salir cuanto antes y para lo que necesita los tres puntos que se ponen hoy en juego. Cogió mucha confianza y moral con su triunfo del sábado pasado contra el Espanyol, más si cabe con el gran juego que realizó. Su idea será volver a repetir éxito en Anoeta para que su campo vaya siendo muy difícil de conquistar por los rivales y sea la base del buen campeonato que desea hacer. Todo apunta a que Matarazzo, que está sancionado, repetirá el mismo once que sumó los tres primeros puntos, ya recuperado Remiro de sus molestias y con los goleadores Barrenetxea y Óskarsson, el asistente Oyarzabal y el resurgido Zubeldia, entre otros. Los fichados Fort y Sarr deberán esperar su oportunidad en el banquillo junto a los jóvenes canteranos por los que Jokin Aperribay y Erik Bretos, presidente y director de fútbol del club txuriurdin, han dicho que se va a apostar este curso. Necesita una victoria cuanto antes para despejar las dudas que ha ofrecido, en lo futbolístico, en el arranque de temporada. Con la plantilla cerrada y sin la dispersión de un mercado de fichajes que puede que haya distraído la atención más de lo conveniente, ya no hay excusas. Marcos Alonso volverá al once, cumplida sanción ante el Athletic, y estrena convocatoria Couhaib Driouech, una de las últimas incorporaciones. Aleix Febas se une a la baja de Borja Iglesias, por lesión. Oyarzabal vs Aspas. Son los líderes de Real y Celta. El capitán txuriurdin buscará firmar su primer gol del curso ante el rival al que más veces le ha marcado en LaLiga, ocho, mientras que la leyenda celeste tratará de hacer el segundo de esta temporada en su cuenta particular, que además sería el décimo ante los donostiarras en toda su carrera. Son dos equipos con buen trato de balón y con armas, más allá de los resultados en este comienzo de LaLiga, para hacer daño al rival. La Real apela al factor campo, pero el Celta ya demostró, sobre todo el curso pasado, lo bien que rinde a domicilio. De hecho, el único punto que tiene lo consiguió en Mestalla, lejos de Balaídos. Un encuentro de complicado pronóstico. Apostamos por las tablas.

articles.title: Rodri y la necesidad innecesaria
articles.standfirst: 'Cuestiones mías', una opinión de Amalio Moratalla
articles.summary: 'Cuestiones mías', una opinión de Amalio Moratalla
articles.body: Voy a intentar explicarme para no salir a boinazos de este razonamiento. Rodri es nuestro capitán, nuestro Balón de Oro, nuestro eje en la Selección, un jugador de leyenda. Este verano se han pegado por él Madrid y Barça, entre otros, y es un lujo tenerle en nuestra Liga, pero veo cómo está el Real Madrid y lo que tiene en mediocampo y cómo está el Barça y lo que tiene en mediocampo, y no sé si para mí sería ‘titularísimo’ —que diría el bueno de Manuel Pellegrini— en ninguno de los dos equipos. Él se decantó por el Barcelona en un momento dado de la negociación y, por lo tanto, le saco de la ecuación del Real Madrid, pero me mantengo con lo de la necesidad innecesaria para el Barcelona. La prueba es que, cuando salió unos minutos el otro día ante el Athletic (28 minutos) y ante el Rayo (27 minutos), el cuerpo no pedía verle en el encuentro. Las cosas le estaban funcionando bien a los de Flick y era como empezar a darle minutos de rodaje, pero ya está. Rodri es un seguro de vida dentro de un campo. Su colocación, sus pases, su presencia y su porte ya son un extra. Con continuidad, como le dio De la Fuente en el Mundial, seguro que acabará siendo el eje de seguridad para el Barcelona, pero me gustaría saber quién se va a quedar en el banquillo para que Rodri lo juegue todo. Y si ha venido para disputar solo los partidos grandes, que es el jugador ideal para ellos, no va a funcionar tan bien. Los jugadores no son grifos que cuando los abres sale agua y cuando los cierras se corta el caudal. Necesitan minutos, confianza y continuidad, y solo en esa situación son capaces de desplegar su máximo esplendor. Es más, durante la competición se ponen en forma y es cuando son letales. De la Fuente se inclinó por Rodri, que empezó regular y acabó como el mejor del Mundial, sentando a Pedri en ocasiones en busca de otras combinaciones, y, en vista del resultado, acertó. Pero quiero saber cómo lo va a hacer Hansi Flick para que todos estén contentos y rindiendo. Un Mundial es un torneo corto, pero la temporada —Liga, Champions, Copa— es muy larga. En principio, más minutos a repartir, pero los partidos importantes son unos pocos. Ahí quiero ver la titularidad indiscutible de Rodri que tanto maneja el código del fútbol de élite.

articles.title: Sobre las canteras de Madrid y Barça
articles.standfirst: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.summary: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.body: Siempre he dudado de la política de cantera del Madrid, que parece destinada a crear jugadores para el mercado y allegar fondos, al contrario de la del Barça, que sigue el propósito fundacional de todas ellas: alimentar a la primera plantilla y comprar fuera sólo lo que no se encuentra. Confieso que este verano hay motivo para las duda, pues el Madrid ha ingresado en torno a 200 millones con las ventas de Nico Paz (60), Gonzalo (40), Víctor Muñoz (20) y un largo etcétera que incluye a Álvaro Rodríguez, Mario Gila, Jacobo Ortega, Álex Jiménez, Valdepeñas, Mario Martín, Fran García… Eso ha dado aire para los fichajes de verano pese al descalabro del estadio, por su coste y su menor rendimiento del esperado, asunto que ha urgido al nuevo y discutible pelotazo en la Ciudad Deportiva, que reportará 370 millones salvo que la oposición lo frene.. Muy distinto es el caso del Barça, cuya primera opción para cada puesto es la cantera. Y le funciona. Del boquete que dejó Bartomeu arrastrado por Messi y su cuadrilla, con lugarteniente, ha salido sobre todo con el recurso a la cantera, que ha surtido en este tiempo importantes titulares, con Lamine Yamal como abanderado, y algunos de paso que apenas recordamos ya, los Jutglá, Marc Guiu, o el más reciente Casadó, vendido al Depor. Cada jugador canterano es un fichaje que no se hace, un dinero que se ahorra. Y en sus inicios tienen unos sueldos más bajos que los fichados de fuera; luego, si triunfan, van exigiendo, pero entran con sueldos apañaditos. Y cada fichaje tiene algo de ruleta rusa. Ahí tenemos el pinchazo de Mastantuono, que es de ayer mismo, y no hay que ir muy lejos para recordar los pinchazos de Odriozola, Illarramendi, Jovic, Hazard, Lucas Silva, Reinier, Endrick… Por ahí se han escapado, entre traspaso y sueldos, unos dineros considerables. La pregunta es por qué al Barça le valen para el primer equipo más que al Madrid, ¿porque los fabrica mejor o porque les ofrece un mejor y más ilusionante desarrollo en la casa? Y ¿qué es preferible, criar un Lamine Yamal o comprar un Diomande?

articles.title: David Soria: "Para batir el récord, he jugado con lesiones, con fiebre, con dolor..."
articles.standfirst: El portero del Getafe atiende a MARCA tras convertirse en el jugador con más titularidades consecutivas en LaLiga (193)
articles.summary: El portero del Getafe atiende a MARCA tras convertirse en el jugador con más titularidades consecutivas en LaLiga (193)
articles.body: David Soria (Madrid, 4 de abril de 1993) atiende a MARCA tras conseguir uno de los récords más complicados en la Primera División de España: ser el jugador con más titularidades consecutivas en la historia de LaLiga con 193 encuentros. El portero del Getafe atraviesa su novena temporada en el Getafe y la sexta seguida bajo palos sin ninguna suplencia. Más, en una campaña que el conjunto azulón atraviesa una ilusionante travesía en Europa para jugar la Conference League. Pregunta: Lo primero, felicitarle por el récord de las titularidades consecutivas, 193. ¿Cuál es el secreto para mantener ese estado de forma durante tanto tiempo, tanto en el terreno de juego como para evitar lesiones? Respuesta: Al final, es lo típico que se dice de cuidarte y trabajar. También, acostumbrarte a un umbral del dolor muy alto. Porque al final de todo, he tenido partidos que he jugado con lesiones, con fiebre, con dolor... Al final es una actitud que siempre he adoptado y que siempre, como yo digo, puedo andar o mantenerme de pie, quiero jugar porque al final esto pasa muy rápido y hay que aprovechar cada minuto. P: Habla de la confianza de los entrenadores durante diferentes etapas en el Getafe. Primero Michel, luego Quique Sánchez Flores y luego Bordalás. ¿Que supone para usted saber que es indiscutible para diferentes técnicos? R: Lo primero, agradecer la confianza a cada entrenador. He tenido la suerte de aprender y que me enseñen algo nuevo. Yo creo que los jugadores siempre están en una etapa de formación. He tenido grandes entrenadores, tanto como Michel, como Quique Sánchez Flores o como Bordalás, que es con el que más tiempo he estado. Espero que la confianza que han depositado en mí, haya sido mutua. P: ¿Qué le supone posicionarse tan arriba en un club de esta magnitud como es el Getafe? R: Yo creo que hay que estar agradecido a todos: entrenadores, presidente, directores deportivos, compañeros... Ellos me han dado la oportunidad de asentarme en Primera División, de crecer y de obtener el récord. Solo tengo palabras de agradecimiento para ellos. Ellos han ido cada etapa confiando en mí. También, cada contrato que hemos ido renovando y bueno, ahora tengo hasta 2030, espero que siga el récord. P: Ha mencionado en varias ocasiones a Bordalás. Desde dentro del vestuario, ¿qué debe saber la gente de él que no se conozca? R: Es una persona muy cercana y muy exigente, pero también tiene muchos momentos graciosos. Hace que la exigencia inconscientemente parezca hasta incluso menos. Es un grandísimo entrenador que le tengo muchísimo cariño. Llevo yo creo siete años con él en los que siempre ha confiado en mí. Siempre hemos conseguido resultados y los objetivos, que al final es lo que importa. P: En esta última temporada al Getafe se le ha identificado como un equipo que juega a la defensa y que tiene un estilo muy agresivo. ¿Hasta qué punto es cierta esa creencia? R: Yo creo que es una batalla perdida. Llevamos desde que llegué hace nueve años con el mismo discurso. Creo que hoy en día todos los equipos hacen lo mismo, no se salva ninguno. Bueno, hay que convivir con ello. Yo siempre digo que la gente se queja cuando les ganas. Preferimos que se quejen, siempre cuando nosotros perdemos nadie se queja del Getafe. Yo la doy ya como una batalla perdida en la que siempre tienes que defenderte. Al final muchas veces se cruza la línea e incluso es una falta de respeto al profesional, porque te quieren quitar mérito. La cuestión es acostumbrarse a las críticas, porque eso significa que ganamos muchos partidos. P: Cambiando ahora a fuera del terreno de juego. ¿Qué opina del proyecto actual del estadio y de cómo está quedando la remodelación? R. El estadio, la verdad, es que es algo sorprendente y yo creo que está ahora mismo a un 33%, no está ni a la mitad de acabado. Es un cambio grande, un cambio que yo creo que era necesario porque la afición también se merece unas instalaciones de Primera y creo que ha llegado un poco tarde, queda un año y medio duro de obra para todos y para ellos. Desde el primer partido, todos estamos un poco asombrados porque parece que estamos jugando en otro campo. No nos da la sensación de estar en el Coliseum antiguo. Queremos poder disfrutar de un campo que, por lo que hemos visto y lo que se está haciendo, yo creo que va a ser de los mejores. P: Hablando de los últimos mercados de fichajes, el Getafe está utilizando un patrón de fichar a jugadores de categorías más bajas (1RFEF), como Uche, Davinci y ahora Francho. ¿Hasta qué punto considera que estos jugadores están preparados para ese salto de categoría a Primera División? R: Hay una cosa llamada fair play financiero en LaLiga que te obliga a tener unas condiciones muy estrictas, en la que equipos como el Getafe, que no tiene tanto poder adquisitivo, tiene que reinventarse y tiene que buscar jugadores en categorías menores para que nos puedan ayudar o hacerles crecer para sacarle rendimiento, incluso pensando en una futura plusvalía, porque al final, aparte de fútbol, es un negocio y creo que es un mercado que si se hace bien, se puede sacar bastante rédito tanto a nivel futbolístico como a nivel económico. Nosotros encantados de todo el mundo que venga a ayudar. Hemos visto a Uche, a Davinci que tiene 18 años, ahora también Francho, que ha venido del Zaragoza, que también es es un gran jugador. Todos los que vengan, da igual la categoría, que vengan a sumar y nosotros encantados. P: Aprovechando el tema de los jóvenes, ¿cree que actualmente se le está exigiendo demasiado llegar a la élite a jugadores con 16 o 17 años, sobre todo en una posición tan complicada como es la de portero? R: Yo creo que en el fútbol, en general desde que yo empecé hasta ahora, surgen los ajustes y problemas económicos de los clubes que provoca que la cantera sea más importante. Creo que los jugadores llegan más rápido. Creo que antes era mucho más complicado llegar a Primera División. Ahora vemos equipos que tienen cuatro o cinco jugadores de cantera, todo se debe a que los clubes quieren correr porque quieren sacar jugadores jóvenes. Quizás se corre un poco o bastante con ellos, también la gente siempre se fija en jugadores como Lamine Yamal, que tiene 19 años, y esos son casos únicos en el mundo. Que tengan paciencia, al final esto es largo. Cuando eres joven y tienes 18 o 19 años, te quedan muchas cosas por vivir. Cuando lleguen, que tengan la capacidad sobre todo de mantenerse, que al final es lo importante. P: ¿Cuál le parece el portero más completo de la Liga? R: Hay grandísimos porteros. Es una cuestión de gustos. Yo creo que Courtois sigue siendo uno de los más completos. Tenemos a Joan García, que está dando un nivel espectacular. Unai Simón, campeón del mundo y titular en la selección. Oblak también aparece. Puedo decir una lista muy larga, creo que el nivel de porteros en España es grandísimo. P: Desde el otro punto de vista, ¿cuál es el delantero que le resulta más incómodo tener delante? R: Yo creo que los delanteros veteranos son los más complicados, por ejemplo, Kike García, Budimir, Muriqi... Luego están los que todo el mundo conoce, Vinicius juega muy rápido. Creo que cada uno tiene sus cualidades y su manera de hacerte gol. P: Desde que llegó al Getafe, ¿cuál ha sido el jugador que más le ha sorprendido? R: Yo creo que hemos tenido grandísimos jugadores. Greenwood fue una grata sorpresa, respecto al nivel de calidad que tenía. Sobre todo, la determinación en el juego que tenía. Puede ser uno de los que más nivel ha tenido y hemos podido compartir. P: ¿Y del vestuario actual? ¿Con qué compañero se queda si tuviera que elegir uno? R. Este año hemos tenido un cambio de ciclo bastante grande, se han ido muchos jugadores y amigos. Creo que tenemos un grupo muy bueno y muy humilde, que todo lo estamos basando en el trabajo. Ahora ha vuelto Enes Unal, con el que ya había compartido vestuario anteriormente. Tengo a Borja Mayoral, que llevo mucho tiempo con él. Tengo grandes compañeros, creo que vamos a hacer un grupo humano bastante bueno. P: Hablando del equipo y del vestuario, ¿cuáles son los objetivos que se propone el Getafe para esta temporada? R: Lo primero creo que es la permanencia. Yo siempre digo, por la experiencia que tengo, que es LaLiga lo que te da de comer. Puedes hacer una buena campaña europea, una muy buena Copa del Rey, pero si en LaLiga no cumples, el objetivo no vale de nada durante el año. Luego disfrutar de Europa, nunca sabes cuándo la vuelves a jugar. Tenemos el mérito de jugarla con el trabajo del año pasado, ya hemos pasado la previa, que era un objetivo primordial. Al final estamos en una liga muy competitiva y es muy difícil jugar Europa. P: Está mencionando Europa. Me gustaría que se pusiera en situación: 2 de junio de 2027, el Getafe en la final de la Conference League en el Besiktas Park. David Soria se prepara para la tanda de penaltis a los 11 metros. ¿Qué le tránsmite ese sueño? R: Lo primero inquietud, sería un sueño. Quiero estar en una final con el Getafe, una final europea, tener la posibilidad de ganarla y ayudar a conseguir un título en esa faceta. La verdad es que es muy bueno que se me está dando la oportunidad. Sería un auténtico placer estar en ese momento. P: Después de tantos años en el Getafe y de conseguir un récord histórico como son las titularidades consecutivas (193), ¿qué le queda todavía a David Soria por conseguir? R: No pienso más allá del próximo partido, de ese día. La experiencia que tengo es ir partido a partido y disfrutar. El fútbol se acaba y cada vez queda menos. Aunque todavía me queda mucho y, si Dios quiere por lo menos ocho o nueve años más. Al final es verdad que yo llego a una etapa ya del desconcierto, que hay que disfrutar porque se va acercando cada vez más el final y tengo grandes compañeros que han ido acabando y te lo dicen: "Al final disfruta que cuando te des cuenta se acabó". Darle como siempre la mayor profesionalidad, intentar ayudar lo máximo posible, disfrutar y conseguir los objetivos del año.

articles.title: Asencio afronta el juicio del vídeo sexual pendiente del perdón de las mujeres afectadas: las claves del caso
articles.standfirst: El defensa del Real Madrid sigue teniendo sobre su cabeza una solicitud de dos años y medio de cárcel por dos delitos contra la intimidad
articles.summary: El defensa del Real Madrid está pendiente
articles.body: El defensa del Real Madrid Raúl Asencio el juicio por el vídeo sexual que presuntamente grabaron tres de sus excompañeros de la cantera del club con dos jóvenes de 17 y 18 años en Gran Canaria, pendiente de que la Fiscalía retire la condena que pide para él. El jugador internacional sigue teniendo sobre su cabeza una solicitud de dos años y medio de cárcel por dos delitos contra la intimidad, pero el Ministerio Fiscal ya ha adelantado que está dispuesto a retirarla si las dos mujeres confirman en el juicio que lo han perdonado, como ya han manifestado en la instrucción. Y ello es posible porque el delito que se imputa a Raúl Asencio tiene el carácter de semipúblico en el Código Penal español y la responsabilidad que cabe exigir a quien lo comete desaparece si el ofendido por lo ocurrido lo perdona; las ofendidas, en este caso. Su defensa tiene atada ya esa salida desde hace meses con los representantes legales de las dos afectadas, que retiraron sus acusaciones particulares contra él tras recibir una indemnización cuya cuantía no ha trascendido y una disculpa formal del jugador. Sin embargo, todo ello se hizo al final de la instrucción, por lo que la fiscal del caso exigió que ese perdón no solo apareciese en un acta notarial (como pretendía la defensa), sino que se formalice en el juicio oral, para que el tribunal pueda cerciorarse de que las dos jóvenes lo conceden de forma consciente y libre. Los hechos sobre los que gira este juicio ocurrieron en el verano de 2023 en un club de playa de Amadores (sur de Gran Canaria), cuando tres compañeros de Raúl Asencio en aquel momento en la cantera del Real Madrid, Ferrán Ruiz, Juan Rodríguez y Andrés García, mantuvieron una relación sexual con dos jóvenes plenamente consentida. El problema es que también tomaron vídeos y fotos del encuentro, presuntamente sin permiso de las dos mujeres. Y luego, según las acusaciones, difundieron esas imágenes por WhatsApp a varias personas más a pesar de que las chicas les dijeron que las borraran. Uno de esos vídeos llegó al teléfono móvil de Asencio, al que se acusa de habérselo mostrado una tercera persona, a sabiendas de que se grabó sin permiso y de que las afectadas exigieron eliminarlo. No ha transcendido si las defensas de Ruiz, Rodríguez y García han intentado también obtener el perdón de las víctimas, pero en su caso solo les libraría de la acusación menos grave que se dirige contra ellos, ya que la Fiscalía también les imputa un delito de pornografía infantil, por grabar y difundir imágenes sexuales de una menor. Y en ese cargo concreto, la ley no permite el perdón del ofendido. Con él o sin él, se condena, si hay pruebas suficientes del delito. Fuentes de las defensas no descartan que el juicio finalmente no se celebre, ya que sigue abierta la posibilidad de que Ferrán Ruiz, Juan Rodríguez y Andrés García pacten una condena de conformidad con la Fiscalía y las acusaciones que representan a las jóvenes, confesándose culpables a cambio una pena menos grave. Si ese acuerdo no se produce, se exponen a solicitudes por parte del Ministerio Público de cuatro años y siete meses de cárcel. La vista se celebra desde las 9.00 horas en la Plaza número 5 de la Sección Penal del Tribunal de Instancia de Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, con tres sesiones previstas (jueves 3, viernes 4 y lunes 7). En principio, ninguno de los cuatro acusados comparecerá en la Ciudad de la Justicia de la capital grancanaria, ya que la juez les ha permitido asistir al juicio por videoconferencia.

articles.title: Eto’o calls on African football federations to support FIFA chief Infantino
articles.summary: Samuel Eto’o says a higher budget might have attracted the likes of Mbappe and Tchouameni to play for Africa instead.
articles.body:
Cameroon Football Federation president Samuel Eto’o has urged African football chiefs to support Gianni Infantino , crediting the FIFA president with accelerating the development of the continent’s associations and allowing more countries to reach the World Cup.

“President Gianni Infantino has changed football,” Eto’o said in an interview with French sports newspaper L’Equipe.

“Mr Infantino has helped our continent. He has helped our federations develop much more quickly, and we have to recognise that. We should support him for everything he has achieved so far.”

His comments contrast with UEFA’s increasingly confrontational position towards the FIFA president, underlining the differing priorities of African and European football leaders.

“He has given opportunities to nations that had never had the chance to take part in the greatest tournament of all, the World Cup,” the former Cameroon forward added.

Infantino said that he would seek re-election at the FIFA Congress on March 18, 2027.

Africa had nine direct places at the expanded 48-team World Cup in Canada, Mexico and the United States this summer, compared with five at the 2022 tournament in Qatar.

UEFA opposed the now-abandoned proposal to transfer commercial rights connected to the men’s and women’s World Cups and the Club World Cup to a new subsidiary, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), with outside investors taking a stake.

While FIFA said the project had been permanently withdrawn, European football’s governing body has continued to challenge its handling of the plan and has sought permission from a US court to obtain evidence for a potential criminal complaint in Switzerland against Infantino and other FIFA officials and advisers.

UEFA also said it would work with partners and stakeholders to propose a new way of distributing resources through the existing FIFA Forward programme.

Eto’o, however, considered that African federations could not be expected to view FIFA policy in the same way as wealthier football nations, as they also relied heavily on government funding.

“When you see some federations with budgets of 150,000 euros, how can they compete against the big countries?” he said. “We will never be able to have the same perception of things as the big countries.”

Eto’o added that the shortage of resources also contributed to African countries losing potential talent to Europe.

“If we in Cameroon had the possibility of relying on a budget of $20m or $40m per year, of course we would have had players like [Kylian] Mbappe and [Aurelien] Tchouameni,” he said, referring to the France internationals, who have Cameroonian family ties.

“UEFA is an important confederation for FIFA. It contributes enormously to football, but it should not be considered the only or the most important confederation,” he added.

articles.title: Ranking the biggest game-changing transfers of the Premier League era
articles.summary: Some transfers take time to bed in, others prove instant game-changers - here are the top 10 signings of the Premier League era that moved the needle.
articles.body:
The 'here we go' is on hold, the 'bombas' are done and dusted and the window panes are reverberating after being forcefully closed on Tuesday night.

Now comes the moment for new arrivals to make their mark on the pitch rather than the balance sheet.

Throughout the Premier League era there have been hordes of transfer hits and misses, but today we're looking at those signings who proved game-changing for their club and the competition, the ones who really moved the needle.

I've ranked my top 10 below. You can have your say in the comments.

You could make an argument for plenty of players who were left off this list. Thierry Henry is probably the one quibbled over the most, Arsene Wenger turning him from misfiring winger to one of the generation's greatest forwards.

But Arsenal had been champions 12 months before he arrived, and it took until Henry's third season for the Gunners to reclaim that crown.

You could point to Cristiano Ronaldo, who won a Ballon d'Or at Manchester United, or Wayne Rooney, who became the club's record goalscorer.

But a teenage Ronaldo took time to bed in, while Rooney, despite a debut hat-trick in Europe, had to wait until his third season for a Premier League winners' medal.

Then there's a plethora of Manchester City signings. Erling Haaland announced himself with 36 goals in 35 top-flight games but arrived in the middle of City's four-year title-winning streak. Yaya Toure, Kevin de Bruyne and Rodri all had big impacts.

However, the list can only be 10 names long. So here it is...

10. Petr Cech - Rennes to Chelsea, £7m, July 2004

Austrian goalkeeper Jurgen Macho was one of first faces through the door as the Roman Abramovich era began at Chelsea, arriving on a free transfer from Sunderland, only to tear his cruciate ligament and never play for the club.

A keeper signed the following summer would prove far more influential at Stamford Bridge.

While prising Claude Makelele from Real Madrid's Galacticos was a huge statement - likewise Hernan Crespo from Inter Milan - Petr Cech was the wall on which back-to-back titles were built.

Cech conceded only 15 goals in his debut league campaign, going on a run of 1,025 minutes without being beaten and ending the season with a record 24 clean sheets.

His Chelsea career spanned 11 seasons and included four Premier League titles and a Champions League. The Blues made back the £7m they paid - and then some.

9. Alan Shearer - Southampton to Blackburn, £3.6m, July 1992

Blackburn Rovers, fresh off a sixth-placed finish in Division Two, immediately set out their intentions after promotion via the play-offs guaranteed them a spot in the inaugural Premier League season.

Southampton striker Alan Shearer had interest from Manchester United, but Rovers - bankrolled by local businessman Jack Walker - tabled a British record £3.6m for the 21-year-old and enjoyed an almost immediate return.

Shearer scored 16 times in his first 21 Premier League games before injury, helping Blackburn finish fourth in their first top-flight season for 27 years. He bagged 31 as they finished runners-up the following term, and 34 in 1994-95 as Rovers were crowned champions for the first time since 1914.

Chris Sutton, another British record buy at £5m from Norwich City, may argue he was the signing who got Blackburn over the line, forming a formidable 'SAS' frontline, but it was Shearer's arrival that set the ball rolling.

8. Carlos Tevez - Corinthians to West Ham, undisclosed, August 2006

West Ham fans frantically refreshing Ceefax on 31 August 2006 must have thought they'd landed on the jokes page when news broke of a double swoop for a pair of Argentina's top young stars.

It was a huge coup for the Hammers, pipping the world's best clubs to add 22-year-olds Carlos Tevez and Javier Mascherano to Alan Pardew's squad.

With West Ham struggling near the bottom of the league, Mascherano left for Liverpool on loan after Christmas. Tevez, meanwhile, would have a huge impact.

West Ham were bottom with 11 games to go - nine points adrift of Sheffield United - but won seven games and Tevez netted seven times, including the winner against Manchester United on the final day, to relegate the Blades.

Sheffield United claimed foul play over the third-party ownership of Tevez and Mascherano, and West Ham were eventually ordered to pay £20m in compensation, having initially been fined £5.5m rather than being docked points.

7. Robinho - Real Madrid to Manchester City, £32.5m, August 2008

It gets somewhat lost in the cloudy narrative of the past, but Robinho had a decent first season at Manchester City, scoring on his Premier League debut and netting 14 times in 31 top-flight games to finish as their top scorer.

Things went downhill from there, but Robinho's performance was less important than what his arrival meant for the future of English football. It was City laying down a marker.

On the day the club were bought by the Abu Dhabi United Group - it also happened to be transfer deadline day - they nabbed one of the world's most prominent players from under the noses of Chelsea for a British record fee.

City finished 10th that season. But 18 years and more than £3bn on transfers later, they have become the most dominant club in England, winning eight titles.

6. Virgil van Dijk, Southampton to Liverpool, £75m, January 2018

Mohamed Salah might feel hard done by here. After all, he did score 32 Premier League goals in his first season at Liverpool after arriving from Roma in 2017.

But that didn't immediately move the needle in terms of pushing Liverpool further up the league table - they finished fourth again and scored only six more goals as a team compared to the previous season.

Instead, it was the £75m signing of Virgil van Dijk in January 2018 - and arguably goalkeeper Alisson Becker that summer too - that really raised the bar for Jurgen Klopp's side, who lost only once the following season and conceded only 22 goals as they racked up 97 points.

Incredibly, Liverpool were beaten to the title by Manchester City, but they became European champions the following season and won a first league title in 30 years a year later.

5. Robin van Persie, Arsenal to Manchester United, £22.5m, August 2012

It was a sign of how the Manchester United and Arsenal rivalry had cooled.

Once the key protagonists in Premier League heavyweight contests, the Gunners would seemingly never contemplate allowing their top scorer to join United.

Yet on the back of a season in which he netted 30 goals to finish as the league's top scorer, Robin van Persie left Arsene Wenger's outfit to line up for Sir Alex Ferguson, who was scorned by Manchester City's emergence and desperate to return the title to Old Trafford.

Van Persie went on to score 26 times as United reclaimed the throne in Ferguson's final season - the club's 20th title - while Arsenal slipped to a distant fourth.

4. Sol Campbell, Tottenham to Arsenal, free transfer, July 2001

A handful of journalists gathered at Arsenal's London Colney training base expecting the unveiling of goalkeeper Richard Wright from Ipswich. Instead they were stunned to see former Tottenham skipper Sol Campbell walk in.

The England defender, who joined Spurs as a youngster more than a decade earlier, had lucrative offers from Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Inter Milan.

There was no inkling that he would end up down the road at Highbury instead, the deal sealed during clandestine meetings with Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger and vice-chairman David Dein.

"I have kept my head when other people around me were losing it," Campbell said at the unveiling of a transfer that was both seismic in the north London rivalry and the direction of the Premier League trophy.

He proved a phenomenal presence at the heart of Arsenal's defence, winning the league and FA Cup double that season and adding another Premier League crown as one of the 'Invincibles' two years later - a title clinched, of all places, at White Hart Lane.

3. N'Golo Kante, Caen to Leicester, £5.6m, August 2015

N'Golo Kante was playing in France's regional amateur leagues until his late teens. Only three years before he joined Leicester City in 2015, the tireless midfielder was turning out in his country's third tier.

The Foxes thought they'd found a bargain, but did not realise quite what an impact his arrival would have.

Kante became the beating heart of Claudio Ranieri's midfield as Leicester went on their astonishing title-winning run. While Jamie Vardy scored the goals and Riyad Mahrez brought the flair, it was the diminutive Frenchman's energy and ability to always be in the right place that set the tone.

Kante missed only one game and made more tackles and interceptions than anyone in the division on his way to becoming a Premier League champion, before Chelsea paid the Foxes almost five times what they nabbed him from Caen for a year earlier.

2. Sergio Aguero, Atletico Madrid to Manchester City, £35m, July 2011

Sergio Aguero set out on his debut as he meant to go on, scoring twice and setting up another in a 30-minute cameo off the bench against Swansea City.

Manchester City were without a top-flight title since 1968 when the Argentine arrived from Atletico Madrid.

Ten months later he had netted 23 goals in 34 Premier League games, including the one deep into stoppage time that crowned City champions.

City had spent lavishly on forwards previously but the prolific Aguero was a game-changer.

His goals shifted the power balance in Manchester and, after a decade in sky blue, he departed as the club's all-time record scorer with 260 goals to complement his five league titles.

1. Eric Cantona, Leeds United to Manchester United, £1.6m, November 1992

Where do you start with Eric Cantona? The maverick Frenchman arrived in England having won the title with Marseille, which was followed by a two-month ban for throwing a ball at a referee and a fallout with the hierarchy.

Advised to move to England, he rocked up at Leeds - via a trial at Sheffield Wednesday - in January 1991 and swiftly helped them clinch the First Division.

A few months into the new season, Cantona's relationship with manager Howard Wilkinson broke down.

Manchester United, languishing in mid-table by late November, without a league title in 26 years and having been dumped out of the Uefa Cup by Torpedo Moscow, came calling - after their bid for Wednesday striker David Hirst was rejected.

Cantona proved a revelation. He scored nine times in 23 games and was influential as United ended up winning the inaugural Premier League title by 10 points.

The forward would win four titles in five years at Old Trafford, including two league and cup doubles, laying the foundations for a generation of success before his shock retirement in 1997.
